headline: Highest risk is compliance/data handling mismatch: Botpress can install packages while awesome-selfhosted is a non-runnable catalog with no shared surfaces, so most interaction risks are low or none.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is non-runnable and exposes no I/O surfaces, while botpress has no documented shared channel to ingest its outputs. With no shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge in either profile, a prompt-injection pathway is not evidenced.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added between the pair, injection risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the pair disconnected from shared copy-paste workflows.
Do not route awesome-selfhosted content into botpress prompts automatically.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a shared channel is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither profile shows data classes touched, network egress is none for both, and no shared workspace or authenticated principal is documented. Without a path for sensitive data to move from one agent to the other or out to a third party, leakage is not supported by the profiles.
conditions: IF either agent is later connected to a shared workspace containing sensitive files, leakage becomes plausible.
mitigations: Avoid placing sensitive files in any shared directory.
Keep both agents on separate local workspaces.
requires-engineering: document and enforce data-class boundaries if sharing is introduced.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is non-runnable and has no write surfaces, so it cannot contend for mutable state. botpress can install packages, but without a shared writable target or concurrency model, the pairwise write-conflict pathway is only possible under unusual external setup.
conditions: IF both agents are given the same writable directory or package environment, conflict risk increases.
mitigations: Avoid concurrent package installs in the same environment.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: botpress is a customer-support agent that could operationalize content, but awesome-selfhosted is only a knowledge-management catalog and is not documented as producing authoritative facts for botpress. With no evidence that botpress treats its output as trusted input, cascading error is limited.
conditions: IF botpress is configured to ingest awesome-selfhosted output as authoritative knowledge, downstream errors become plausible.
mitigations: Require human review before botpress acts on catalog-derived content.
Label awesome-selfhosted output as untrusted reference material.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before any action-taking step.

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either profile, and both show no data classes touched. Because compliance risk would require a specific regulated data flow that is absent here, the pair is not evidenced to violate compliance controls.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into either agent, compliance review is required.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Document retention and residency before any sensitive deployment.
requires-engineering: map data flows to applicable compliance controls if regulated data is added.
